title: Risotto con Pancetta e Piselli
subtitle: Pancetta and pea risotto
excerpt: Risotto con pancetta e piselli is a simple, satisfying everyday risotto: salty, crisp pancetta against sweet peas in a creamy Parmesan-finished rice. It is the kind of risotto made in Italian homes on a weeknight, when there is not much in the fridge but the storecupboard is stocked.
sourceNotes: Pancetta and pea risotto is a standard of domestic Italian cooking across the north. It is quick, inexpensive, and uses ingredients that are almost always in the fridge or freezer.

content.text: This is one of the easier risotti to make: the pancetta fries at the start before the onion goes in, which means you only need one pan. The peas go in towards the end so they stay bright and sweet rather than collapsing into the rice.

items.prepNote: taste first -- the pancetta is salty

content.text: Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a heavy pan over a medium-high heat. Add {{pancetta}} pancetta and fry for 4 minutes until lightly golden. Remove half the pancetta with a slotted spoon and set aside for garnish.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add {{onion}} onion to the same pan and cook in the rendered fat for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed.

Add hot {{chicken-stock}} stock a ladleful at a time, stirring and waiting for each addition to absorb. After 12 minutes, add {{peas-frozen}} peas. Continue adding stock for a further 6 minutes until the rice is al dente.

Remove from the heat. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter and {{parmesan}} Parmesan. Season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Rest for 1 minute. Serve topped with the reserved pancetta.

items.symptom: The peas are khaki and mushy
items.fix: Add frozen peas only in the last 5 to 6 minutes of cooking. They need only long enough to heat through, not to cook.

content.text: Pancetta and pea risotto is a standard weeknight dish in northern Italy. It does not have the prestige of a risotto alla Milanese or a seafood risotto, but it is one of the most eaten versions. The combination of salty cured pork and sweet peas in a creamy, Parmesan-finished rice is deeply satisfying and very fast to make once the technique is learned.
